Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
744 PM EDT Tue Sep 15 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 233 PM EDT Tuesday...

The forecast for the upcoming weekend has trended drier.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 233 PM EDT Tuesday...

1. Dry and seasonable before a few showers Thursday.

2. Chances for showers decreasing this weekend, but remaining 
seasonable cool.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 233 PM EDT Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Surface high pressure is shifting off to the 
east, and return southerly flow has developed. Winds will 
increase this afternoon and gusts in the 10-20 mph range are 
expected heading into the evening. A dying cold front will push 
down from the north overnight and bring the chance of a couple 
showers. However, weak forcing and dry air in the low levels 
should cause most of this to fall as virga, though a few 
sprinkles are expected in northern areas. Dry and warm weather 
will return for Wednesday with highs in the 70s to around 80. An
area of rain will attempt to move into the region on Thursday 
into Thursday night as isentropic lift occurs on a warm front. 
EPS ensemble members generally favor a wetter solution and a 
farther north front, while GEFS and CMCE members generally keep 
the rain to the south. Models have shifted into a bit more of an
agreement where it looks like at least southern Vermont should 
see a few showers, but the northward extent remains uncertain. 
However, any precipitation would be light and stratiform, with 
the wet EPS probabilities of a half inch of rain generally 
ranging between 20-30 percent.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Following a washed out cold front by the end of the work 
week, trends have continued to move towards the ECMWF solution 
keeping most, if not all, precipitation south of the area Saturday 
night and Sunday. The baroclinic zone responsible for the area of 
potential showers will be draped more over central and southern New 
York with better forcing southwest of our region. That said, model 
solutions Sunday afternoon into Monday denote a subtle redevelopment 
of a surface low off the southern New England coast which could 
bring some light shower chances to southern Vermont. All in all, our 
shower chances this weekend are trending lower. Our flow pattern 
will remain confluent into next week with zonal flow aloft with 
generally dry conditions towards next week. Model solutions begin to 
vary by early next week in terms of precipitation chances. An upper 
level high over the Great Lakes will set up a dry corridor from the 
Great Lakes into northern New England, while a moisture axis over 
the Mid Atlantic attempts to push north. Model uncertainty in how 
much dry air there is will determine if moisture and associated 
shower potential are able to penetrate northward into our region, or 
if dry subsident air keeps our shower chances shunted to the south. 
Regardless, zonal northwesterly flow will keep our temperatures 
through the weekend into early next week on the seasonably cool side 
with highs fairly consistent in the mid to upper 60s, and lows in 
the low to mid 40s, with some cold hollows hovering about the upper 
30s. Sky conditions favor mainly cloudy conditions through the 
extended.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Through 00Z Thursday...VFR with local MVFR expected through the
TAF period. Current ceilings AOA 8000 ft will gradually lower
overnight as a weak cold front pushes across the region from
west to east. Clouds will lower to 3500-5000 ft, except at SLK
where ceilings will drop to 2500 ft. These conditions will
persist through 16z Wed, then expect gradually lifting ceilings
thereafter. A few very light rain showers will be possible with
the frontal passage, but no visibility restrictions or
significant impacts are expected, so mention in the TAFs is not
warranted at this time. Winds light S/SE this evening will
occasionally become gusty overnight, mainly at BTV as a weak low
level jet moves east. This jet may also bring a period of
marginal LLWS overnight, as well, particularly at SLK/MSS. Winds
turn to the W/SW and eventually NW during the day Tuesday 
behind the frontal passage. 


Outlook...

Wednesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Slight
chance SHRA.
Friday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Saturday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Sunday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.

&&

.MARINE...
Channeled southerly flow will continue to increase this 
afternoon and evening. They should ramp up on the broad waters 
into the 20 to 25 knot range by late afternoon, and near 20 
knots over the northern waters. As a result, waves will markedly
increase into the 1 to 3 feet range by this evening. During the
evening, they will likely reach the 3 to 4 feet range in the 
vicinity of Colchester Reef and 2 to 3 foot range in the Inland 
Sea as winds will likely peak in intensity. Elevated south winds
will likely persist into Wednesday morning before sharply 
diminishing by Wednesday afternoon.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
